'''Georgi Bliznakov''' ({{langx|bg|Георги Близнаков}} (14 November 1920 – April 2004) was an eminent<ref>{{cite news |title=National Assembly President Gerdjikov expressed his condolences to the family of Academician Bliznakov |url=http://www.parliament.bg/index.php/?page=newsa&lng=en&SType=show&id=334 |work=[[National Assembly of the Republic of Bulgaria]] |date=16 April 2004 |accessdate=16 June 2009 }}</ref> [[Bulgaria]]n [[chemist]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Who's who in Science in Europe: A Biographical Guide in Science, Technology, Agriculture, and Medicine |volume=4 |publisher=Longman |year= 1991 |edition= 7th |page=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/47/mode/2up?view=theater 47] |isbn=9780582086623 |url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/n3/mode/2up |url-access=registration |via= [[Internet Archive]]}}</ref> He was head of the Department of [[Inorganic Chemistry]] and rector<ref name=Todorovsky>{{cite journal |last=Todorovsky |first=D. |year=2004 |title=110 years Department of Inorganic Chemistry in St. Kliment Ohridski University of Sofia |journal=Annual of the University of Sofia Faculty of Chemistry |volume=97 |issue=1 |pages=7–18 |url=http://www.chem.uni-sofia.bg/annual/pdf/Tom97-2004_book1.pdf}}</ref> at [[Sofia University]], director of the Institute of Inorganic Chemistry of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] and vice-chairman of the academy.<ref>{{cite journal |year=2008 |title=On the 60th anniversary of Physical Chemistry Department |journal=Journal of the University of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=169–176 |url=http://www.uctm.edu/journal/j2008-1/26_Conference_169-176.pdf |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081203030516/http://www.uctm.edu/journal/j2008-1/26_Conference_169-176.pdf |archivedate=2008-12-03 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Bliznakov was born in 1920 in [[Berkovitsa]], Bulgaria. After graduating in chemistry in 1943 from Sofia University he worked in industry until 1946, when he joined the [[University of Varna]] as an assistant in inorganic and [[physical chemistry]]. In 1949 he joined the Department of Physical Chemistry at the Polytechnic Institute in [[Sofia]] (now the [[University of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy]]) as an assistant where he stayed until moving to the Department of Inorganic Chemistry at [[Sofia University]] in 1951, becoming full professor and head of department in 1960. He stayed in that post until 1989, serving as university rector from 1981 to 1985.<ref name=Lazarov>{{cite journal |last=Lazarov |first=D. |year=2004 |title=115 years of university inorganic chemistry |journal=Annual of the University of Sofia Faculty of Chemistry |volume=97 |issue=1 |pages=19–30 |url=http://www.chem.uni-sofia.bg/annual/pdf/Tom97-2004_book1.pdf}}</ref>

==Academic interests==
Bliznakov's main area of research was [[crystallization]]. He was the first to introduce [[adsorption]] as a [[thermodynamic]] factor in crystal growth, and studied [[catalysis]], particular in relation to [[ammonia]] [[oxidation]],<ref name=Todorovsky/> the preparation of [[pure substance]]s, [[radiochemistry|radiochemical]] processes,<ref name=Lazarov/> and the effect of impurities on the linear crystallization rate.<ref name=Djarova>{{cite journal |last=Djarova |first=M. |year=2004 |title=A century of investigations in the domain of crystallization processes in the Department of General and Inorganic Chemistry at Sofia University |journal=Annual of the University of Sofia Faculty of Chemistry |volume=97 |issue=1 |pages=43–66 |url=http://www.chem.uni-sofia.bg/annual/pdf/Tom97-2004_book1.pdf}}</ref>

He is the co-author of some of the most popular secondary school chemistry text books in Bulgaria.<ref name=Todorovsky/>
